name: DocVQA
description: DocVQA is a large scale dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images. It consists of 50,000 questions defined on 12,767 document images sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library. The dataset covers a multitude of different document types including tables, forms, figures, and a range of textual, graphical and structural elements. Questions are categorized into 9 types based on reasoning requirements.
creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
publisher: CVIT, IIIT Hyderabad, India; Computer Vision Center, UAB, Spain
citeAs: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar. DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images.
rai:dataCollection: Document images were sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library. Documents were downloaded from different collections and pages were hand-picked for use in the dataset. Binarized images were minimized and pages with tables, forms, lists and figures were prioritized. Questions and answers were collected with the help of remote workers using a web-based annotation tool in a three-stage annotation process.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Web API
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Documents from the UCSF Industry Documents Library (https://www.industrydocuments.ucsf.edu/), spanning 6,071 industry documents from 5 industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, and chemical), covering documents from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Documents span from 1900 to 2018; most documents are from the 1960-2000 period.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Binarized images were minimized in the dataset. Pages with tables, forms, lists and figures were prioritized over pages with only running text. The data is split randomly in an 80-10-10 ratio to train, validation and test splits.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: OCR tokens were extracted using a commercial OCR application. For BERT QA models, OCR tokens recognized on document images were serialized to a single string separated by space in top-left to bottom-right order. Answer spans were approximated by finding the first match of the answer string in the serialized OCR string, following an approach proposed in TriviaQA.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation was organized in three stages. Stage 1: Workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs, with answers entered verbatim from the document. Workers were encouraged to add more than one ground truth answer per question where warranted. Stage 2: A different worker was shown the image and questions (without stage 1 answers) and required to enter answers and assign one or more question types to each question. Workers could flag questions for language issues or ambiguity. Stage 3: If no answers from stage 1 matched any answers from stage 2, the question was sent for review by the authors, who could edit questions and answers before accepting or ignoring them.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: If none of the answers entered in the first stage match exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the question is sent for review in a third stage. Questions flagged as inapt due to language issues or ambiguity are not included in the dataset. The third stage review is done by the authors themselves.
rai:annotationsPerItem: At most 10 question-answer pairs per document image; multiple ground truth answers per question were encouraged where warranted; question types assigned during stage 2.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Commercial OCR application (used for extracting OCR tokens from document images)
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, code and leaderboard are available at docvqa.org. No explicit versioning or deprecation policy is described.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Document images may contain personal information such as names of people, institutions, places, addresses, ZIP codes, phone numbers, and employee names, as these are sourced from real industry documents.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to inspire a 'purpose-driven' approach in document image analysis and recognition research, driving methods that use low-level cues (text, layout, arrangements) and high-level goals (purpose, relationship, domain knowledge) in solving problems of practical importance.
rai:dataBiases: Most documents are from the 1960-2000 period. The dataset uses many documents from food and nutrition related collections as they have a good number of non-binarized images. Documents come from only 5 industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, and chemical). A large majority of questions start with 'what is the', asking for date, title, total, amount or name. Almost all top answers are numeric values.
rai:dataLimitations: Majority of documents in the UCSF library are binarized and binarization has taken a toll on image quality. OCR errors can result in wrong answers even when models correctly ground questions. Models struggle with questions requiring understanding of figures, diagrams, handwriting, and document structure. The dataset is limited to documents from 5 specific industries.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation, and Testing of Visual Question Answering models on document images. The dataset is split 80-10-10 for train (39,463 questions, 10,194 images), validation (5,349 questions, 1,286 images), and test (5,188 questions, 1,287 images) splits. It can also be used for benchmarking reading comprehension models on document images.
